title: L&D: current and proposed organisation

organisation.label: Meridian Components (fictional)
organisation.scope: A seven-person L&D team supporting 4,800 people across five plants.

organisation.context: Every company detail, role, quantity and answer in this worked example is fictional. CHRO is shown outside the seven-person L&D headcount. Current AI use is absent.

levers.name: Reporting
levers.current: Head has two direct reports; four indirect reports.
levers.proposed: Head has three direct reports; three indirect reports.
levers.reason: Move Digital Learning Specialist to Head of L&D, subject to CHRO agreement. Headcount stays seven.
levers.basis: Authored fictional L&D exercise; no real participant or company claim.

levers.name: Centralisation
levers.current: Operations Manager clears each booking list.
levers.proposed: Routine bookings follow standing rules; exceptions return to Operations Manager.
levers.reason: Centralise the rule while delegating bounded action.
levers.basis: Authored fictional L&D exercise; no real participant or company claim.

levers.name: Span of supervision
levers.current: People supervise people; no agents operate.
levers.proposed: Two human supervisors oversee two agent services; active run counts remain untested.
levers.reason: Agent roles and simultaneous runs are different from human direct reports.
levers.basis: Authored fictional L&D exercise; no real participant or company claim.

levers.name: Standardisation
levers.current: Templates exist; people interpret checks and chase submissions.
levers.proposed: Explicit roster checks, allowed slots and evidence fields govern delegated work.
levers.reason: Consistent rules support delegation; learning quality still needs review.
levers.basis: Authored fictional L&D exercise; no real participant or company claim.

levers.name: Specialisation
levers.current: Coordinator spends time on booking and chasing.
levers.proposed: Coordinator concentrates on incomplete cases; partners judge practice.
levers.reason: Task changes do not imply eliminating a role.
levers.basis: Authored fictional L&D exercise; no real participant or company claim.

levers.name: Coordination
levers.current: Email handoffs between design, operations and plant partners.
levers.proposed: Shared exception and evidence queues pass clear outputs to named people.
levers.reason: Cross-function handoffs need an owner and a condition for completion.
levers.basis: Authored fictional L&D exercise; no real participant or company claim.

readiness.validation: Check job relevance and exclude confidential employee records.
Use a sandbox calendar and invented roster; verify allowed actions, logs and stop control.
Measure time reviewing exceptions rather than assuming oversight is free.
Review proposed Digital Learning Specialist reporting line.

pilot.scope: Four weeks with one fictional 30-person supervisor cohort; sandbox roster and calendar only. Test drafting and booking separately; human process remains authoritative.
pilot.measure: Compare preparation time, booking accuracy, exception-review time and assessed material quality.
pilot.baseline: Not measured. Record the current process for a comparable cohort before comparison.
pilot.success: Proposed: no unauthorised invitations, every seeded exception caught, acceptable material quality and less total coordination effort including review.
pilot.stop: Stop on an out-of-cohort invitation, unapproved content, missed seeded exception or exposure of personal data.
pilot.review_date: After four weeks; broader use and reporting change need separate agreement.

open_questions: Would the CHRO approve the proposed reporting change and access scope?
Can the LMS and calendar support the required checks and stop control?
What baseline and review capacity does the first trial establish?

history.initial_choice: Fictional manager initially favours automating scheduling and follow-up.
history.ai_proposal: Keep diagnosis, content approval and readiness judgement with humans; delegate bounded administrative actions.
history.participant_decision: Authored simulated choice accepts a sandbox trial and changes follow-up to evidence collection only.
history.note: No real participant confirmed this record. It is a fictional worked example.

comparison.perspective: Fictional Head of L&D. Can reallocate work and agree a limited test; CHRO approves reporting changes and technology access.
comparison.scale: Seven L&D people shown as seven role nodes, plus their CHRO. Two partner roles cover five plants; they are not five additional teams.

organisation.current_note: Current: people and the LMS perform the work; no AI is in operational use.
organisation.proposed_note: Proposed: human-led learning with bounded agent work. Seven L&D staff remain.

proposed.label: Design assistant
proposed.detail: Human + AI assistant. The Design Lead prompts the assistant, checks all material and approves its use. This is human-directed assistance; it has no delegated action permissions.

proposed.label: Cohort operations
proposed.detail: Human + agent for nomination checks; Agent only for eligible bookings. Operations Manager supervises; Digital Learning Specialist maintains the service. Head of L&D owns the outcome. Only approved cohorts and slots are permitted; exceptions return to Operations Manager.

proposed.label: Practice follow-up
proposed.detail: Human + agent. North Partner supervises the shared collection service; both partners judge evidence and coach managers. Digital Learning Specialist maintains access and records. No employee scoring or appraisal writes are permitted.

exercise.staffing_review: The Head of L&D keeps all seven L&D posts. Agents take routine nomination checks and bookings, but the Programme Coordinator still resolves incomplete nominations and cases outside the agreed rules, so no post is removed. The Digital Learning Specialist moves to report to the Head of L&D, which needs the CHRO's agreement.
